subject: SIG: Consolidating KMS/HSM rotation ops and evidence — questions & next steps
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy@acme-corp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: rotation windows, BYOK/HSM evidence request

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Acme is compiling SIG artifacts ahead of our procurement review and we need a few clarifications for the encryption section before we mark items as "answered":

1) Rotation cadence: clearly state the default rotation cadence for service-managed KMS keys (CMKs) used for data-at-rest and for envelope keys.
2) BYOK/HSM: is there a supported BYOK workflow where the customer imports a non-exportable key into an HSM under our service? If yes, what evidence do you provide that keys remain non-exportable?
3) In-transit: can you confirm TLS versions and whether mutual TLS is available for private deployments?
4) Audit logs / proof: what audit artifacts can you share for recent rotations (timestamps, actor IDs, and verification checks)?

We'd appreciate a short packet (PDF/word) and an answer sheet so our reviewer can mark each SIG question as closed. Can you get this back by EOD 4/12?

Thanks,
Lucy Chen
Security Manager, Acme Analytics
security@acme-corp.com

--
Acme — Procurement (SIG queue)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: rotation windows, BYOK/HSM evidence request

Hi Lucy — thanks for the clear list. I attached a draft rotation matrix and a concise answers doc (see attachments) and put the short answers inline below. We can finalize wording after Grace validates the HSM language.

Quick answers (high level):
- Rotation cadence (service-managed): CMKs used to envelope customer data are rotated automatically every 365 days by default; envelope keys used for ephemeral workloads rotate on a 30–90 day cadence depending on retention profile. Manual rotation can be triggered by customer request.
- BYOK/HSM: We support customer-supplied keys for Private deployments via an HSM-backed import flow where keys are marked non-exportable at import. For Hosted customers we offer a BYOK integration where the customer's KMS is federated (keystore never leaves customer control).
- Evidence for non-exportability: We can provide HSM import job metadata, import logs with job IDs, and signed import confirmations from the HSM provider showing key attributes (non-exportable flag).
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ is enforced; TLS 1.3 supported. Private deployments can be configured for mTLS between customer VPC endpoints and the control plane.
- Audit logs: We can provide redacted rotation audit logs containing timestamps, operator IDs (internal service account IDs), and rotation status; full unredacted logs require an NDA and a justified scope.

Attachments: redwood_kms_rotation_matrix_v2.pdf (matrix + example audit rows), sig_answers-encryption-2028-04-11.docx (SIG Q&A formatted).

Grace and Dev — can you confirm the phrasing around the HSM import confirmation (non-exportable evidence) and whether we can include a sample signed import artifact in the packet?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Commercial Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Lucy Chen <lucy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: rotation windows, BYOK/HSM evidence request

Eve / Lucy — quick technical clarifications from the ops side:

- Default automated rotation is implemented as a managed job in our key-service; the job creates a new envelope key, re-wraps active object keys within a consistent maintenance window (typically 02:00–04:00 UTC), and emits an audit event. The 365d/30–90d numbers Evelyn quoted are policy defaults configurable per-customer.
- HSM import flow (private): we use the vendor import APIs that generate an import-wrapping key; the import job returns an import job artifact (importJobId + signature) and we persist that metadata in the key-service. The HSM marks the imported key non-exportable at the HSM level.
- Evidence we can attach: sample import job record (redacted), the importJobId verification entry from the HSM provider, and a snippet of the audit event stream showing rotate/create events.

My ask: Grace / Marcus — can we include a redacted importJobId example and the exact import confirmation wording the HSM provides? Lucy, if that meets your reviewer's needs we can include both in the packet.

-Dev
Senior Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Lucy Chen <lucy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: rotation windows, BYOK/HSM evidence request

Thanks — confirming we can provide the following artifacts for SIG intake:

1) redacted HSM import confirmation: includes importJobId, timestamp, and a signed statement from HSM that the key is non-exportable. We'll redact customer-identifying fields but leave importJobId intact for audit traceability.
2) rotation audit snapshot: CSV export of rotation events (timestamp, keyId, actorId, operation, result) for the last 90 days. Sensitive operator emails will be replaced with service-account IDs.
3) TLS/MuTLS statement: formal sentence for the SIG entry confirming TLS1.2+ and mTLS availability for Private deployments.

We should avoid sharing raw key material — we will not provide raw key bytes or any private key material. We can include a short paragraph describing key custody models and link to our technical runbook.

I attached the answers doc with the suggested language edits (sig_answers-encryption-2028-04-11.docx). If Acme needs full unredacted logs for a compliance audit, we'll require a scoped access request and an approved NDA + SOW.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Lucy — attaching the finalized packet per your timeline. Highlights:
- redwood_kms_rotation_matrix_v2.pdf: concise table showing default cadences, maintenance windows, and sample audit rows.
- sig_answers-encryption-2028-04-11.docx: SIG Q&A formatted per your list (rotation, BYOK, in-transit, audit artifacts).

Short summary for your reviewer:
• Default rotation: CMKs 365 days; envelope keys 30–90 days depending on workload; maintenance window typically 02:00–04:00 UTC. Manual rotations available on request.
• BYOK/HSM: supported in Private deployments via HSM import; imported keys are marked non-exportable by the HSM. Hosted BYOK achieved via KMS federation where the keystore remains customer-controlled.
• Evidence: redacted HSM import confirmations (importJobId + signed import attributes) and rotation audit snapshots (timestamp, keyId, actor service-account ID). Full unredacted logs require an NDA + scoped request.
• Transport: TLS 1.2+ required, TLS 1.3 supported; mTLS option available for Private deployments.

If this looks good I'll drop the Drive link to the packet and you can confirm closure of the SIG questions. Happy to join a short call if the procurement reviewer wants walk-through.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Commercial Security Operations
Redwood Inference
